title: Berry–Esseen bound with nonzero means
statement: Let $\{X_i\}_{i\in\iota}$ be a finite family of independent, measurable real random variables on a probability space, each with finite second moment. Suppose the sum of their variances is positive and each centered variable $X_i-\mathbb{E}X_i$ has finite third absolute moment. For every $x\in\mathbb{R}$, the absolute difference between the cumulative distribution function of $\sum_i X_i$ at $x$ and that of the Gaussian with mean $\sum_i\mathbb{E}X_i$ and variance $\sum_i\operatorname{Var}(X_i)$ is at most $C\,\sum_i\mathbb{E}|X_i-\mathbb{E}X_i|^3/(\sum_i\operatorname{Var}(X_i))^{3/2}$, where $C$ is the third-moment Berry–Esseen constant.
hypotheses_covered: Each variable has finite second moment
The sum of variances is positive
Each centered variable has integrable third absolute power
